properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 13 at 3:44AM PST until November 13 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of
15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously
large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of
40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash
over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey
Bay.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon.
For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM today to 4 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is
specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.

infrastructure.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding
expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous
surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Clatsop County Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon today to 4 PM
PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from noon today
to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak this evening and tonight. In addition, the
Astoria Tide gauge is forecast to reach approximately 10.6 ft
during high tide this afternoon.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night.
Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at
elevations above 2,500 feet with mainly a dusting to half inch on
grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow
accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black
Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in
the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of
Highway 160  near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on
Friday night.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 9:44AM AKST until November 13 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and mixed precipitation expected. Total snow
accumulations from 2 to 10 inches.

* WHERE...Kodiak Island Northeast.

* WHEN...From 6 PM this evening to 6 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heavy snow and rain on snow may create difficult travel
conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A compact storm will move southeast of Kodiak
Island tonight and remain nearly stationary through Friday
afternoon to evening. Slight deviations in the storm position to
the east and west will cause snow levels to fluctuate between sea
level and 400 ft in elevation. Kodiak city and the archipeligo to
the north are most likely to mix with rain at times, resulting in
total snow accumulations of 2 to 4 inches. If rain does not mix in,
expect higher snow totals. Areas from Kodiak Airport to Women's Bay
are more likely to maintain a northwest wind, resulting in colder
temperatures, a lower likelihood of rain, and snow accumulations
from 6 to 10 inches.
properties.instruction:

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 12 at 1:42PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at
higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night.
Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at
elevations of 2,500 feet, mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and
elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations
are possible over the highest portions of Big Black Mountain. The
snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could
yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160
near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on Friday night.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

11/14, and 0.6 ft above normal (5.0 ft MLLW) at 7:50 PM Sun
11/15.
